image_description: A close-up studio shot of a bicycle disc brake assembly against a white background. The image features a silver metallic rotor with circular ventilation holes and a black caliper mechanism mounted to the frame/fork. A black cable housing is visible entering the caliper.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is clearly circular and thin relative to its diameter, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A mechanical housing (caliper) is positioned over the outer edge of the rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The center mounting interface appears to be a 6-bolt or Centerlock adapter typical of bicycles, not the large circular lug nut pattern found on automotive disk brakes. This is a domain mismatch with the taxonomy prior which describes car brakes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is perforated with holes for ventilation/weight reduction, fitting the 'ventilated' criteria broadly, though it lacks the specific 'two plates with fins' structure of automotive rotors.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The brake pads are internal to the caliper housing and are not directly visible in this external view.
The line entering the caliper is a black sheathed cable housing, indicating a mechanical cable-actuated system, not a hydraulic hose.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface features distinct circular drilled holes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The metal surfaces appear clean and uniformly silver/grey, showing no signs of thermal bluing or brown oxidation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper body has the texture and form factor of cast metal (likely aluminum alloy).

artifact_observations.location: Black vertical support arm/frame on the left side
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is white text printed vertically on the black component. While it mimics branding, the characters are indistinct and slightly malformed, resembling AI-generated pseudo-text rather than a clear brand logo.

artifact_observations.location: Cable entry point at bottom left of caliper
artifact_observations.reasoning: The black cable housing seems to merge slightly into the caliper body without a distinct ferrule or stopper, creating a minor structural ambiguity.

Boundary sharpness between rotor holes and background
